summary: Iteration 14 — per-page permissions feature tested end-to-end. Backend: 14/14 pytest pass (test_iteration14.py): PATCH /api/users/{id}/permissions enforces super_admin-only (403 for office_admin), 400 on super_admin target, 400 on invalid level, persists via /auth/me. /auth/login + /auth/me responses include the `permissions` dict. require_edit dependency correctly returns 403 on POST/PATCH/DELETE for view/none and lets GET through for students, clients, transactions, expense_requests; PATCH /api/auth/me is gated by settings perm. Super admin bypasses all checks. Newly registered office_admin gets DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS (all-edit) and approval-handler also seeds defaults if missing. Frontend: super_admin → /users → Approved tab shows 16 cards each with [data-testid=permissions-<id>] (visible only on approved office-admins, not super-admin rows). Clicking opens [data-testid=permissions-dialog] with all 7 perm-row-* rows × 3 chip levels. After saving students=view + clients=none and re-logging in as blr1: nav-clients HIDDEN, nav-students visible, add-student-btn HIDDEN. After saving expense_requests=view + transactions=view: new-request-btn HIDDEN, add-transaction-btn HIDDEN, no edit-*/delete-* row buttons. FOUND + FIXED a critical crash bug in Transactions.jsx — `allowEdit` was referenced but never defined; added the missing `const allowEdit = canEdit(user, "transactions")` line. After fix, page renders for both super_admin (Add transaction + edit/delete row icons visible) and blr1-view (no write controls, no crash). blr1 permissions restored to all-edit at the end.

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED by testing agent: `allowEdit` referenced on lines 105/204/205 but never declared, causing an uncaught ReferenceError that crashed the entire Transactions page for every user. Added `const allowEdit = canEdit(user, 'transactions');` near the other useState declarations to match the pattern used in Students/Clients/ExpenseRequests.

action_items: (none — testing agent already fixed the Transactions allowEdit crash. Main agent should review the one-line addition in Transactions.jsx.)
critical_code_review_comments: models.PERMISSION_PAGES is a tuple and DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS is built from it — clean, used consistently in auth.register, users.update_approval, users.update_permissions.

auth_lib.require_edit defaults a missing key to 'edit' which is the right back-compat behaviour for users created before the feature shipped. Super_admin role check happens BEFORE the perms lookup — correct.

users.update_permissions rebuilds the permissions map from PERMISSION_PAGES rather than blindly persisting the payload — prevents arbitrary keys from being stored and rejects unknown levels with 400. Good.

users.update_approval seeds DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS only when target.permissions is missing — does NOT clobber an admin who later re-approves a user whose permissions were previously customised. Correct behaviour.

Transactions.jsx had a missed change in iteration 14: `allowEdit` was referenced without being declared (Students/Clients/ExpenseRequests all declare it, only Transactions missed it). Fixed by testing agent. Recommend a lint rule (eslint no-undef) to catch this class of bug — react-app preset usually catches it; check whether the warning was being suppressed.

permissions feature is refreshed only on next login — documented in agent-to-agent context note. Users.jsx dialog description says 'Changes take effect on their next page load' which is slightly inaccurate (it's actually next login since useAuth caches user). Consider adding a refresh-me call or websocket push so changes apply immediately, OR update the wording to 'next sign-in'.

When clients=none is set, /clients nav hidden but the route still works if visited directly (no client-side route guard). Acceptable per spec but worth flagging — backend GET /api/clients is intentionally not gated and front-end relies on sidebar hiding only.

PermissionsUpdate model uses `permissions: dict` without Pydantic-level validation; route handler does the validation manually. Functional but a Literal-typed nested model would make the OpenAPI schema cleaner.

Testids added in iteration 14: permissions-<id> (per approved card), permissions-dialog, permissions-list, perm-row-{overview|quick_entry|transactions|clients|students|expense_requests|settings}, perm-{page}-{edit|view|none}, perm-reset, perm-save. The permissions list endpoint (GET /api/users?status=approved) currently returns 16 approved users in this env — be aware when filtering by email. Note that user.permissions is refreshed on next login (cached in useAuth), so toggling permissions for a user already in a session requires sign-out/sign-in.
rca of the issue: Transactions.jsx crash: developer added perms-gating around the add-transaction button and per-row edit/delete buttons (`{allowEdit && ...}`) but forgot the corresponding `const allowEdit = canEdit(user, 'transactions');` declaration that the other three pages (Students, Clients, ExpenseRequests) all have. ReferenceError thrown during render → entire /transactions route crashes for ALL users (not just office_admins with restricted perms). Mitigation: added the missing declaration directly under `const currency = ...` line 20. Verified: super_admin and view-only blr1 both render without crash; blr1 sees no write controls.
